# Desktop-GL entry points an X server's GLX dispatch table references.
#
# TAWC's libhybris backend answers `libGL.so.1` with a GLES-only shim (see
# scripts/build-libhybris.sh "GL shims"). That is deliberate — the project
# policy is "no desktop GL", GLES via EGL is the only client GL. But a shim
# that is *functionally* GLES-only must still be *ABI*-complete: a binary
# whose DT_NEEDED names libGL.so.1 and whose relocations reference desktop-GL
# entry points dies at exec with `undefined symbol`, before any of its own
# code runs and long before the NULL-glX probes can steer it to EGL.
#
# The rootfs Xwayland is exactly such a binary: Xorg's GLX server module is
# generated against the Linux OpenGL ABI, so it references the whole GL 1.2 +
# ARB_multitexture surface whether or not indirect rendering is ever used.
# build-libhybris.sh emits a no-op stub for each name below that libhybris's
# own GLESv2 does not already define, so those binaries load and fall through
# to EGL like everything else.
#
# Regenerate against a distro libGL and an X server, inside a rootfs:
#   nm -D --undefined-only /usr/bin/Xwayland | awk '{print $NF}' \
#     | grep -E '^gl[A-Z]' | grep -v '^glX' | sort -u
# Every name here is GL 1.0-1.2 fixed-function, the ARB_imaging subset, or
# ARB_multitexture. Nothing modern belongs in this file: a shader-era symbol
# stubbed here would let a probe conclude the entry point works and call it,
# which is strictly worse than failing to find it.
glAccum
glActiveTextureARB
glAlphaFunc
glAreTexturesResident
glBegin
glBitmap
